shots.text: 1492. Everyone warned Columbus he'd sail off the *edge.*
Except... *nobody said that.*
Medieval people knew the Earth was *round.*
Around 240 BCE, Eratosthenes *measured it.*
With shadows and a *stick.*
Pretty close. How close depends on *his units.*
Medieval scholars kept copying it for *centuries.*
Universities taught from a book called *On the Sphere.*
Kings even held a little round *Earth.*
The Earth: still *round.*
The real argument? The Earth's *size.*
Columbus thought it was *way smaller.*
The experts said he'd run out of *food.*
The experts were *right.*
He survived because America was *in the way.*
So who invented the flat part? *Washington Irving,* 1828.
A Columbus biography. With *extra drama.*
Later writers repeated it. Textbooks *loved* it.
The Earth: still *round.*
Anyway, here's the *myth* again.
